agentenv_review.result: No newer portable park/wake optimization applies to the gVisor combined-state volume. The post-v0.1.2 direct OverlayBD packaging work is coupled to AgentEnv's Firecracker memory-snapshot path. The production pin already contains the shared bounded cache, warm ublk pool, and compact correctness/performance fixes.
agentenv_review.background_download_decision: Retained. Whole-layer prefetch would contend with demand reads and download untouched bytes from the combined writable-filesystem/application-memory volume.

changes.unchanged_import_fast_path: A detached wake now preserves authenticated artifact identities when only Linux st_dev changed after the ublk remount, then discards the empty temporary COW and restores the existing remote publication authority.
changes.parallel_s3_verification: The snapshot config GET and layer HEAD requests use a bounded eight-worker verifier instead of serial layer checks.
changes.implicit_sdk_wake_commit: Successful SDK activity that wakes a parked sandbox now atomically changes the gateway route to running, clears obsolete snapshot authority, and releases its durable snapshot reference.
changes.benchmark_instrumentation: The live benchmark can wake through sandbox-scoped SDK exec and retain node restore-phase timings.

promoted_snapshot_canary.note: The first wake is the empty-cache observation; the second is the immediately following warm-cache observation. A two-sample median is intentionally not used as the steady-state claim.

caveats: These are qualification observations, not latency percentiles.
The sandbox is deliberately small; multi-GiB dirty working sets and concurrent wake bursts still need separate load measurements.
Park and detach each contain an Object Storage write and show transient tail outliers even though their medians are stable.
The optimization removes redundant import work; it does not remove the real new delta produced by the next park.
